questions.q: What is a filename~ backup created by a text editor?
o: An encrypted copy of the original file stored under /tmp
An automatic backup saved as the original name plus a tilde
A compressed archive of the whole web application tree
A changelog of every edit made during that editor session
questions.x: Editors such as Vim and Emacs append a tilde to the filename. Editing CustomTemplate.php can create CustomTemplate.php~. That copy is a backup of the file being edited.
questions.h: The backup is the original name with one extra character. Which character is appended?

questions.q: Why can editor backup files be a problem on a production web server?
o: They may be served as plain text and leak the original source code
They run automatically as soon as the HTTP server process starts
They overwrite live application files on every incoming request
They always contain hardcoded admin passwords in the first line
questions.x: Backup files are often deployed by accident. Depending on web server configuration, a request for the ~ file may return the source as plain text instead of executing it.
questions.h: The risk is disclosure, not execution. What might the server send back if it treats the backup as a static file?

questions.q: If you edit CustomTemplate.php, what backup name might the editor create?
o: CustomTemplate.bak.php in a hidden .backup folder
CustomTemplate.php.orig at the web server document root
CustomTemplate.php~ sitting next to the original PHP file
template~CustomTemplate.php in the editor swap directory
questions.x: The usual pattern is the original filename with a tilde appended, so CustomTemplate.php becomes CustomTemplate.php~. Anyone who can request that path may receive the backup.
questions.h: The partial uses this exact example. What single character is added, and where is it added?

questions.q: Which statement about editor backup files is correct?
o: A tilde suffix marks the backup file
Backup files cannot be fetched
Servers always run .php~ as PHP
None of these statements are true
questions.x: The first statement is true. Editors append a tilde, so CustomTemplate.php~ is the backup. The other two are false. None is wrong because that suffix claim is true.
questions.h: Is the tilde added at the start of the name, or at the end?

questions.q: Why might a web server return source for CustomTemplate.php~ but not for CustomTemplate.php?
o: PHP files on disk are encrypted, and only the ~ copy is plaintext
The .php file is executed, while .php~ may be served as static text
Requests to .php are blocked, while ~ files skip access control
The original file is empty, and the backup holds the only copy
questions.x: A typical server runs .php through the PHP interpreter and returns only the output. A ~ backup may not be treated as PHP, so the server can send the file contents as plain text.
questions.h: One path is handled as code. The other may be handled as a static file. Which suffix is less likely to be executed?
